title: lock: re-arm fingerprint reader after a missed or errored scan
author: slr01
body:
# PR: Re-arm lock screen fingerprint reader after a missed/errored scan

File: `shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml` (lock plugin)

## What & why

One Quickshell `PamContext` is reused for the whole lock. After its first
session completes or errors, `fingerprintPam.active` never returns to false,
so `startFingerprint()` never starts another scan. Fingerprint unlock is at
most one attempt per lock — a single miss or driver error disables the reader
until you unlock with the password.

This change:

- Replaces the single `PamContext { id: fingerprintPam }` with a `Component`
  factory; each attempt creates a fresh instance (`fingerprintPamInstance`),
  so a miss/error no longer kills the reader for the lock.
- While the display is blanked (`runBlank`) it stops the retry timer and gates
  `startFingerprint()` on the existing `displaysBlank` state, so no new scan
  starts while blanked (without this some drivers, e.g. the Broadcom 58200
  TOD, scan continuously and hit a thermal self-disable). An in-flight scan is
  allowed to finish: aborting the pam session on blank severed a scan the
  reader was still servicing, and since the reader is not a compositor wake
  source that left it dead until password unlock.
- Re-arms on wake (`runWake`).
- Stops the fingerprint flow while a password prompt is in flight.

No new configuration is required. Behavior without a reader configured is
unchanged (`fingerprintConfigured` false → never started).

## How to apply

```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/quattro -b fix/lock-fingerprint-rearm
patch -p1 < lock-fingerprint-rearm.patch
git add shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml
git commit -m "lock: re-arm fingerprint reader after a missed or errored scan"
# push and open a PR against quattro
```

Validated on Omarchy 4.0.4 with a Broadcom ControlVault 3 reader
(`0a5c:5843`, fprintd 1.94.5): after a first-scan error, subsequent scans
succeed, including after a multi-minute locked+blanked period followed by wake.

## Suggested commit message

```
lock: re-arm fingerprint reader after a missed or errored scan

The lock screen reused one Quickshell PamContext for every fingerprint
attempt. Once its first session completed or errored, PamContext.active
stayed set, so startFingerprint() never started another scan: at most one
fingerprint attempt per lock, and a single miss disabled the reader until
password unlock.

Create a fresh PamContext per attempt via a Component factory, stop scanning
while the display is blanked (gating on the existing displaysBlank state) and
re-arm on wake, and suspend the fingerprint flow while a password prompt is
in flight.
```
